### App version

3.1.1.4

### Feature or improvement you want

Hi there

I've come across the issue where, once AntennaPod has saved chapters into the database, that there is almost no possibility to refresh those chapters from the feed (or file)

In my case I've pushed wrong chapter markers via the RSS feed by mistake and corrected them after a while and realized that they only appear when I create a new subscription of the podcast, as chapters are pretty statically cached in the SimpleChapters table of the database.

During my investigation I've found that there has been a refresh episode chapters functionality in #6177 but as far as I understand this only reloads them from database which is misleading, since it doesn't actually refetch from the feed.

I wonder if it would make sense to just remove the cached SimpleChapters from the database when the episode is deleted (this way it would reload it when an episode is downloaded again). I feel this would also be a good tradeoff for not putting too much stress on the database (by adding and removing things) and would be somewhat logical that chapters are not sticking around after an episode is removed from the device.

This would free us from having a "clear cache" logic somewhere in the UI which would just be clutter for an edge-case.

### Why should this be added?

Remove the cached SimpleChapters entries

### App version

3.11.4

### Feature or improvement you want

Currently, AntennaPod allows sorting episodes by date, title, etc., but does not allow per-podcast customization for where new episodes are automatically added in the "Up Next" queue (top or bottom).

### Why should this be added?

I have daily podcasts where I want new episodes to always appear at the top of the queue, so I can listen to them as soon as possible.
I have other podcasts (e.g., entertainment, storytelling) where I prefer new episodes to be added to the bottom of the queue, so they don’t interrupt my current listening order.

#### Benefits:
* Greater flexibility for users who follow podcasts with different priorities.
* Maintains AntennaPod’s simplicity, as the option would be per-podcast rather than global.

#### Current Workarounds:
- Manually adding episodes to the queue (not practical).
- Using global sorting by date/title, which doesn’t solve the priority issue per podcast.

### Screenshots / Drawings / Technical details

Add a per-podcast setting (e.g., "New episodes position in queue") with two options:
- "Add to top of queue" (default)
- "Add to bottom of queue"

 This setting would be independent of the global episode list sorting.

Android Auto has a "For You" surface that media apps supply content to. ### App version

Android 17

Google Pixel 10 Pro (reproducible on any device)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use AntennaPod by streaming (do not download episodes).
2. Subscribe to enough podcasts that a browse list (e.g. the Inbox-backed "For You", or the Episodes list) contains many un-downloaded episodes.
3. Connect to Android Auto (or the Desktop Head Unit) and open that list.

### Expected behaviour

The list of episodes appears promptly.

### Current behaviour

The list never loads — Android Auto shows a loading spinner indefinitely.

The cause is that building a browsable list resolves every item's final playback URL up front: `MediaItemAdapter.fromPlayable` calls `RedirectChecker.getFinalUrl`, a blocking network request, for any episode without a local file (plus a blocking artwork load). For a streaming user every item is non-local, so opening a list of N episodes fires N sequential network requests on one thread, which can exceed Android Auto's browse timeout. The work is also wasted, because the playback URL is resolved again from the media id when an item is actually selected (`enrichMediaItems`).

issues.title: Vulnerability: Intent URI Injection and High-Fidelity Phishing via OPML Import
issues.body:
### Description
A critical vulnerability was identified in the `OpmlImportActivity` that allows for Intent URI Injection. This flaw can be exploited to bypass the Android sandbox (reading internal database files) or to inject malicious RSS feeds that impersonate trusted podcasts for phishing.

### Vulnerability Details
- **Affected Component:** `de.danoeh.antennapod.activity.OpmlImportActivity`
- **Root Cause:** The activity is exported and processes incoming `Intent` data URIs without validation of the scheme or origin.
- **Exploit Scenarios:**
  1.  **Sandbox Bypass:** Forcing the app to read internal private files like `Antennapod.db` using `file://` URIs.
  2.  **Trust Hijacking:** Injecting a malicious RSS feed that impersonates a trusted podcast. Since the feed is displayed within the trusted AntennaPod UI, attackers can lure users to phishing sites via the 'Visit Website' (globe) icon.

### Proposed Mitigations
We have implemented a multi-layered defense-in-depth strategy:

1.  **Technical Hardening:** Set `android:exported="false"` for `OpmlImportActivity` in `AndroidManifest.xml`.
    ```xml
    <activity android:name=".activity.OpmlImportActivity" android:exported="false">
    ```
2.  **URI Validation:** Explicitly block the `file://` scheme and internal data paths (`/data/data/de.danoeh.antennapod`).
    ```java
    if ("file".equalsIgnoreCase(uri.getScheme())) return false;
    ```
3.  **Identity Verification:** Cross-reference imported feed URLs with the iTunes/Apple Podcasts API to detect impersonators.
4.  **Outbound Link Protection:** Implement a security interceptor/confirmation dialog when users click links from unverified feeds.

### Device model

OnePlus 9 Pro

### First occurred

Started to notice this issue after updating to current version

### Steps to reproduce

The common trigger is: rapidly navigate in and out of the audio player screen while a podcast is playing. The more subscribed feeds you have, the longer getFeedCounters holds the connection, widening the window.

### Expected behaviour

_No response_

### Current behaviour

AntennaPod crashes with a fatal ART runtime abort (Too many inflation attempts) caused by excessive SQLite lock contention when multiple threads simultaneously attempt to acquire the single database connection. The crash is a native SIGABRT that kills the process immediately with no Java-level exception.

Crash Signature

```
F noeh.antennapod: monitor.cc:1125] Too many inflation attempts
F noeh.antennapod: runtime.cc:714] Runtime aborting...
F libc: Fatal signal 6 (SIGABRT), code -1 (SI_QUEUE)
```

Root Cause

PodDBAdapter.openDb() called newDb.disableWriteAheadLogging() immediately after obtaining the writable database. This forced SQLite into rollback journal mode, which permits only a single database connection at a time. All reads and writes — regardless of which thread initiates them — must serialize through that one connection by acquiring the same SQLiteConnectionPool monitor lock.
